cohort: The study included the birthing population in the United States from the National Inpatient Sample (NIS) dataset between 2016 and 2018.
finding: The study found that 2.7% of the birthing population had a primary or secondary diagnosis of substance use disorder (SUD), and these individuals showed statistically significant differences in severity, mortality, procedure type, delivery method, and cost of care compared to those without SUD.
mod_finding: Substance use disorder was associated with statistically significant differences in delivery method.
